components.name: Decisive Button
components.description: The full-width forward action used to start or advance cooking.
components.css: .ds-decisive-button { width: 100%; height: 60px; border: 0; border-radius: 30px; background: #C84F13; color: #F3F0E8; font: 600 15px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 0 24px; } .ds-decisive-button:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-decisive-button:active { filter: brightness(.92); } .ds-decisive-button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #C9A442; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Current Step Tray
components.description: The dominant cream reading field for the current cooking instruction.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-step-tray { background: #F3F0E8; color: #083224; border-radius: 28px; padding: 22px; } .ds-step-tray span { font: 600 17px/23px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-step-tray h2 { margin: 10px 0; font: 600 52px/50px 'Barlow Condensed', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-step-tray p { margin: 0; font: 18px/26px system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Step Preview
components.description: A compact previous, next, or then row that navigates steps without changing timers.
components.css: .ds-step-preview { width: 100%; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; text-align: left; border: 0; border-radius: 18px; background: #F3F0E8; color: #083224; padding: 12px 16px; } .ds-step-preview span { grid-column: 1; color: #C84F13; font: 600 15px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-step-preview strong { grid-column: 1; font: 600 17px/23px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-step-preview b { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1 / span 2; align-self: center; font-size: 24px; } .ds-step-preview:hover { background: #E6DFD2; } .ds-step-preview:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #C9A442; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Static Chip
components.description: A compact equipment or recipe tag with a quiet material outline.
components.css: .ds-static-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 36px; box-sizing: border-box; border: 1px solid #D1C3B0; border-radius: 10px; background: #F3F0E8; color: #083224; padding: 8px 12px; font: 600 15px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Portion Chip — Selected
components.description: The selected portion mode, using the same yellow as active timing.
components.css: .ds-portion-chip { min-height: 48px; border: 1px solid #D1C3B0; border-radius: 24px; background: #C9A442; color: #083224; padding: 0 16px; font: 600 15px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-portion-chip:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-portion-chip:active { filter: brightness(.92); } .ds-portion-chip:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #C84F13; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Timer Control
components.description: A tactile timer well with a large clock and two circular controls.
components.css: .ds-timer { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border-radius: 22px; background: #083224; color: #C9A442; padding: 16px; } .ds-timer div { flex: 1; display: grid; } .ds-timer span { font: 600 17px/23px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-timer strong { font: 700 40px/1 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-timer button { width: 56px; height: 56px; border: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: #234633; color: #F3F0E8; font-size: 26px; } .ds-timer button:hover { background: #346A53; } .ds-timer button:active { transform: scale(.96); } .ds-timer button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #C9A442; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
MealOS feels like a prepared kitchen station. Deep green enamel holds persistent working state while warm cream trays make instructions and ingredients immediately readable. Yellow is reserved for active timing, and burnt orange marks the decisive action that moves the cook forward.

The system is tactile, confident, and practical: large condensed action language, human-scale controls, generous working surfaces, and flat tonal layering that can survive a busy kitchen. It rejects generic dashboard grids and decorative food-blog styling; its identity comes from purposeful trays, shelves, rules, and controls rather than ornamental imagery.
keyCharacteristics: Deep enamel workspace with warm cream prep surfaces.
Condensed, heavy action typography paired with calm Material body type.
Yellow timing state and burnt-orange completion state.
Large trays, compact rounded previews, pills, and circular controls.
Minimal shadow; depth comes primarily from tonal and material contrast.

rules.name: The Two Warm Signals Rule
rules.body: Yellow means timing or active progress; burnt orange means a decisive action. Do not swap their jobs.

rules.name: The Cream Is for Reading Rule
rules.body: Use cream as a prepared content field against enamel, not as a decorative accent scattered through the interface.

rules.name: The Arm's-Length Rule
rules.body: The current cooking action gets the display scale; supporting details stay in the Material hierarchy and must not compete with it.

rules.name: The Enamel Layer Rule
rules.body: Establish depth with adjacent tonal surfaces before adding elevation; never introduce glass, glow, or decorative drop-shadow stacks.

dos: Do preserve cream reading trays against the deep enamel station.
Do keep yellow tied to timing/progress and orange tied to decisive action.
Do reflow cooking mode from balanced panes to one column at the observed 720 dp threshold while preserving working state.
Do keep primary touch controls generous, with circular timer controls at 56 dp and standard Material icon targets elsewhere.
Do use Material 3 navigation, fields, chips, dialogs, and system Back behavior as the native interaction foundation.
donts: Don't turn the interface into a generic dashboard or uniform card grid.
Don't use food-blog photography, bespoke recipe illustration, glass effects, or decorative shadow stacks as the system's identity.
Don't add a permanently visible navigation rail; protect the unfolded cooking workspace with the hidden drawer.
Don't shrink instructions into label-sized type or let secondary controls compete with the current cooking action.
